question: Alberta Independence Referendum: Margin of Victory
resolution_criteria:
Alberta is scheduled to hold a provincial referendum on October 19, 2026. Question 10 asks: "Should Alberta remain a province in Canada, or should the Government of Alberta commence the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution to hold a binding provincial referendum on whether or not Alberta should separate from Canada?"

For the purposes of this market, "Remain" refers to the option that Alberta should remain a province in Canada, and "Leave" refers to the option that the Government of Alberta should commence the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution to hold a binding provincial referendum on separation.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between "Remain" and "Leave" on Question 10.

The “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by "Remain" and "Leave". Percentages will be determined by dividing the number of valid votes each option receives by the sum of all valid votes cast on Question 10.

If "Leave" receives more valid votes than "Remain", this market will resolve to "Leave wins".

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher margin bracket.

If "Remain" and "Leave" receive the exact same number of valid votes, this market will resolve to "Remain <20%".

This market will resolve based on the results of the vote once the count has been made official. If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the referendum is officially rescheduled to a date prior to December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, the same rule applies to the new ballot and its corresponding deadlines. If the results of the referendum are not known definitively, or no qualifying referendum vote occurs, by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other.”

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official results of the vote as published by the Government of Alberta, including Elections Alberta (https://www.elections.ab.ca/); however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

"Other" means any option not listed here.
research:
I've finished the research and am writing up the report now. Everything below uses only information from on or before 2026-10-17.

## 1. Resolution source
- The deciding source is the official results from Elections Alberta ([elections.ab.ca](https://www.elections.ab.ca/)). Its page lists advance voting from Oct 13 to 17, a special-ballot receipt deadline of Oct 16, and election day on 2026-10-19. As of the cutoff, no official Question 10 results existed.
- 2026-09-04: Elections Alberta said it expected about 85% turnout. [CTV](https://guelph.ctvnews.ca/calgary/video/2026/09/04/elections-alberta-expecting-85-per-cent-turnout-in-referendum/)

## 2. Current status
- As of 2026-10-17 the vote had not happened, so nothing is settled yet. The bracket that matters is the margin among valid votes only, so polling numbers need to be recalculated without undecideds. On that basis most polls point to a margin of roughly 48 to 56 points, which is "Remain 40-60%". Two online panels, Angus Reid and Mainstreet, point to roughly 31 to 32 points, which is "Remain 20-40%". The deciding question is which of these two groups of pollsters turns out to be right.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-13 to 17: Advance polls were open. Global News reported 174k ballots cast in the advance period, but I couldn't confirm which date that figure covers. [Global News](https://globalnews.ca/news/12102619/albertas-referendum-draws-174k-ballots-advance-polls/)
- 2026-10-08: The Hub said polls had barely moved since May, with Leave at about 20 to 25% and Remain at 65 to 70%. It warned that pollsters may undersample voters without degrees, who are more than twice as likely to back separation, and that turnout could shift the result. It cited Quebec 1995, where polls showed about 53% Leave and the result was 50.6% No, and Brexit. [The Hub](https://thehub.ca/2026/10/08/polls-suggest-separatists-will-lose-albertas-referendum-but-polling-history-is-full-of-surprises/)
- 2026-05-21: Premier Danielle Smith added the remain/separate question as Question 10, using wording from Thomas Lukaszuk's pro-Canada petition. A Leave win would only start a process toward a later binding vote. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Alberta_independence_referendum)
- 2026-05-13: The Court of King's Bench struck down the Stay Free Alberta separatist petition because Indigenous peoples had not been properly consulted. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Alberta_independence_referendum)

## 4. Base rates / polling
Polls on the official wording, with my calculation of the margin among decided voters ([Wikipedia poll table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Alberta_independence_referendum)):
- 2026-10-14 to 16, Leger: 74 Remain / 21 Leave / 4 undecided, about 56-point margin
- 2026-10-15 to 16, Mainstreet: 65.6 / 34.4, about 31-point margin
- 2026-10-13 to 16, Ipsos: 70 / 23 / 7, about 51-point margin
- 2026-10-13 to 15, Angus Reid: 66 / 34, 32-point margin
- 2026-10-02 to 15, Pollara: 73 / 23, about 52-point margin
- 2026-10-07 to 13, Abacus: 68 / 24 / 8, about 48-point margin
- 2026-10-02 to 04, Leger: 70 / 22, about 52-point margin
- 2026-09-08 to 21, Janet Brown: 72 / 23, about 52-point margin
- 2026-09-18 to 22, Ipsos: 70 / 20, about 56-point margin
- 2026-08-10 to 13, Angus Reid: 61 / 33, about 30-point margin
- 2026-05-22 to 24, Angus Reid: 60 / 35, about 26-point margin
- Trend: Remain support was stable or edging up from May to October. Angus Reid and Mainstreet consistently show Leave about 10 points higher than the other pollsters. That house effect alone moves the implied margin across the 40-point bracket line.
- Other trackers put the weighted average around 75 / 25 among decided voters, a margin of about 50 points. [MaplePolls](https://www.maplepolls.com/referendum), [albertaelections.com](https://albertaelections.com/referendum)
- Historical comparisons: in Quebec 1995 the polls overstated the separatist side slightly. In Brexit 2016 they understated Leave by a few points. [The Hub](https://thehub.ca/2026/10/08/polls-suggest-separatists-will-lose-albertas-referendum-but-polling-history-is-full-of-surprises/)

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-10-09: The Polymarket "Margin of Victory" market opened, with brackets matching this question. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/alberta-independence-referendum-margin-of-victory)
- About 2026-10-14: an aggregator snapshot reportedly showed "Remain 40-60%" at about 54%, the favourite. I couldn't get a full price history or the other brackets' prices from before the cutoff. [PredScope](https://predscope.com/event/alberta-independence-referendum-margin-of-victory)
- I found no Kalshi, Manifold or expert numeric forecasts for the margin itself.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-10-17: last day of advance voting.
- 2026-10-19: referendum day. Question 10 was expected to be counted first.
- The official results announcement is expected around 2026-10-29, which matches the question's resolution date. A recount could delay it.
- Key uncertainties:
  - Turnout: Elections Alberta expected about 85%. Nenshi argued that low turnout would help motivated separatists.
  - Which pollsters are accurate: Angus Reid and Mainstreet versus Leger, Ipsos and Pollara.
  - How spoiled or blank ballots are treated, since they are excluded from valid votes.
